Palmer Luckey says analysts claiming it's too expensive to manufacture in the US are lying to protect megacorps

"I think I have a more realistic view than almost anybody. One of the problems with all these analysts that are telling you that it's going to cost $37,000 to build an American iPhone or $100,000 to buy an American computer."

"They're trying to prop up a status quo that the megacorporations want to keep going. They want to outsource everything. They want to hire cheaper non-American labor." 

"They are willing to say and do anything to convince you that it can't be fixed, that it can't come back, that America is this helpless, neutered, post-relevant empire, and it is just not the case."

"How do I know that? Because I have to make stuff in America every day because I work in the defense industry. The stuff that Anduril makes every day is not actually that different from a computer. My drones are basically computers. They have memory, a GPU, a CPU, sensors, batteries, a rugged integration."

"The only difference between an Anduril attack drone and a laptop is a keyboard and a screen. That is not that hard to figure out, especially for a guy like me who started Oculus and comes from the consumer electronics space." 

"We're not going to let people lie about what America can and can't do anymore. We're just going to do it."
quoted.text_zh:
帕尔默·拉基 (Palmer Luckey) 表示，分析师声称在美国制造成本太高，这是为了保护大型企业而撒谎

“我认为我比几乎任何人都有更现实的观点。所有这些分析师的问题之一是，他们告诉你，制造一部美国 iPhone 需要花费 37,000 美元，购买一台美国电脑需要花费 100,000 美元。”

“他们试图维持巨型企业想要继续发展的现状。他们想要外包一切。他们想要雇用更便宜的非美国劳动力。” 

“他们愿意说、做任何事来让你相信，它无法修复，它无法卷土重来，美国是一个无助的、被阉割的、后相关的帝国，但事实并非如此。”

“我怎么知道这一点？因为我每天都必须在美国制造东西，因为我在国防工业工作。Anduril 每天制造的东西实际上与计算机没有什么不同。我的无人机基本上就是计算机。它们有内存、GPU、CPU、传感器、电池和坚固的集成。”

“Anduril 攻击无人机和笔记本电脑之间的唯一区别是键盘和屏幕。这并不难理解，特别是对于像我这样创立 Oculus 并来自消费电子领域的人来说。” 

“我们不会再让人们在美国能做什么和不能做什么的问题上撒谎。我们只会这么做。”

quoted.text:
this might be my last normal tweet before biotech goes vertical

i'm not a whistleblower. I don't work at Lilly, Novo or any of the big labs

but there is a massive shift happening in human biology right now. 

it's sitting in press releases and almost nobody reads them

the last 6 months alone:

- a once-daily pill roughly doubled median survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer (13.2 vs 6.6 months)
- a one-time gene editing infusion cut hereditary angioedema attacks 87%, and 62% of patients stayed attack-free and off all other prevention for 6 months
- a one-time gene edit for cholesterol dropped LDL up to 62%, and it held for over a year
- a personalized mrna vaccine beat keytruda alone in a 1,137 patient melanoma phase 3
- retatrutide hit ~28% weight loss in a phase 3
- an ai-designed drug entered phase 3
- a pill that regrows hair passed its second phase 3
- an immunotherapy that could let some rectal cancer patients skip surgery, chemo and radiation just got fda approved
- a man lived 271 days off dialysis on a pig kidney
- human cells were caught passing chromosome-sized chunks of DNA to their neighbors, and it changes how the neighbors behave

we are on the verge of an era where the human body is a software problem and the update cycle gets shorter everyday

stick around, it's going to get weird

bio/acc

我们正处于一个时代的边缘，人体是一个软件问题，更新周期每天都在缩短

tweets.text:
One of the best things about Apple was not what they made, but what they chose not to make. 
You knew their top of the line product was going to be a great product all around, with the right trade-offs for a typical user. You didn’t have to look through four or five different models and figure out which was for you. You could just buy the product without even trying it and know that you would love it and it would delight you. 
These days it’s more confusing. Should I buy an iPhone Pro, iPhone Duo, iPhone Pro Max, iPhone Air or iPhone SE? 
Should I get a Macbook Pro, or a Macbook Pro OLED with touch, or a Macbook Neo or a Macbook Air? 
Apple used to have strong opinions about things. A phone shouldn’t require a stylus. A laptop shouldn’t have a touch screen unless we can make it great. We’re not doing a foldable unless it can be truly great. 
Now they are following the market, whereas before they defined the market. They told us what the future looked like, built it for us, and the rest of the industry followed. 
I hope one day Apple can recapture some of that former glory. But right now the AI industry is rewriting what it means to use a personal computer while Apple sits on the sidelines with Siri.

quoted.text: The reason people feel so impassioned about the Apple Touchscreen MBP is because they actually want Apple to make cool stuff. Nobody would care otherwise. Indifference is the worst thing Apple could hope for. If people have passionate responses, they still care. There's a serious lack of cool hardware, especially new cool hardware, and people want to feel enthusiasm and excitement about products again. Products that actually enhance their lives. 0 to 1 moments. Apple used to provide that. The modern man yearns for the innovation. It lets them feel excited for the future in a future that there is increasingly less to be excited about.
quoted.text_zh: 人们之所以对 Apple 触摸屏 MBP 如此热情，是因为他们实际上希望 Apple 制造出很酷的东西。否则没有人会关心。冷漠是苹果最糟糕的希望。如果人们有热情的回应，他们仍然会关心。酷硬件尤其是新的酷硬件严重缺乏，人们希望再次感受到对产品的热情和兴奋。真正改善他们生活的产品。 0到1的时刻。苹果曾经提供过这样的服务。现代人渴望创新。这让他们对未来感到兴奋，而未来的兴奋点越来越少。

tweets.text_zh:
苹果最好的事情之一不是他们制造了什么，而是他们选择不制造什么。 
您知道他们的顶级产品将成为一款出色的产品，并为典型用户提供正确的权衡。您不必浏览四五个不同的型号并找出哪个适合您。您无需尝试就可以购买该产品，并且知道您会喜欢它并且它会让您高兴。

我应该购买 Macbook Pro、带触控功能的 Macbook Pro OLED、Macbook Neo 或 Macbook Air？ 
苹果曾经对事物有强烈的看法。手机不应该需要手写笔。笔记本电脑不应该有触摸屏，除非我们能让它变得很棒。除非它真的很棒，否则我们不会做可折叠产品。

我希望有一天苹果能够重拾昔日的辉煌。但现在人工智能行业正在改写个人电脑的使用意义，而苹果则对 Siri 袖手旁观。

tweets.text:
Tesla’s Optimus training regime leak.

Workers in its Palo Alto R&D facility have been holding “robot university” for many months already. Press got it wrong when they said it just started up.

Workers are wearing 24 lb suits with up to 40 cameras and grids of 3D sensors. To capture very detailed video and 3D fields of whatever the worker does. 

There are multiple configurations.

They are given different tasks to do. They don’t know where the tasks come from.

Multiple squads are working on three shifts 24 hours a day. Similar efforts were seen at the Texas factory.

The data collection effort is immense.

A Tesla car only has nine cameras.

This leads to a data flywheel that is orders of magnitude more data than the car captured.

Separate teams are capturing home data, like making a sandwich, while other teams capture jobs on factory floor, like installing HVAC systems in cars.

Elon isn’t playing around.

I can’t tell you how I learned this.

工人们穿着 24 磅重的套装，配备多达 40 个摄像头和 3D 传感器网格。捕捉工作人员所做的任何事情的非常详细的视频和 3D 场。

tweets.text: What Uber does to their drivers is horrible

quoted.text:
i’m deleting @Uber and moving to @Waymo absolutely 

today, my uber driver told me he has four children living in a garage, and that of the $30 i paid for the ride, he was only getting $7.

it’s the 5th time an uber driver has confronted me about tipping him in cash. this time, he pointed to my diamond earrings and trench coat as evidence that i could obviously afford to pay him more.

NHTSA announced today that they are proposing new rules aimed at removing U.S. federal regulatory barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as @Tesla's Cybercab.
The proposed changes include:
• Eliminating requirements for manually operated turn signal controls in vehicles without steering wheels or pedals: "NHTSA has concluded that the self-canceling and manually operated control requirements in the current standard are unnecessary for turn signal operating units that are installed on vehicles without manually operated driving controls."
• Allowing autonomous driving systems to control turn signals, hazard lights, and high/low beams without traditional driver-operated switches.
• Removing certain dashboard indicator requirements for turn signals and high beams in vehicles without manual driving controls.
• Allowing optional cyan-colored exterior lights to indicate when a vehicle is operating autonomously, with standardized requirements for their placement, brightness, and operation.
• Eliminating outdated restrictions on vertical headlight arrangements, giving automakers greater design flexibility.
• Allowing modern integrated headlights to be tested at manufacturer-specified voltages rather than requiring 12.8 volts.
NHTSA says the changes are intended to eliminate unnecessary regulatory barriers, reduce costs, and enable innovation without compromising vehicle safety.

• 允许在制造商指定的电压下测试现代集成车头灯，而不是要求 12.8 伏。

NHTSA 表示，这些变化旨在消除不必要的监管障碍、降低成本并在不影响车辆安全的情况下实现创新。
